games.title: Classify It!
games.skillName: Giving reasons for classifying plants and animals
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe how living things are classified into broad groups according to common observable characteristics and based on similarities and differences, including micro-organisms, plants and animals; give reasons for classifying plants and animals based on specific characteristics
games.instruction: Read the question, then tap the reason a scientist would give.
games.hint: Not quite. Pick the feature that ONLY that group has, then try again.

questions.ask: Why is a whale classified as a mammal, not a fish?
Why is a bat classified as a mammal, not a bird?
Why is a penguin classified as a bird?
Why is a spider not classified as an insect?
Why is a snake classified as a reptile?
Why is a frog classified as an amphibian?
Why is a fern not classified as a flowering plant?
Why is a pine tree classified as a conifer?
Why is a mushroom not classified as a plant?
Why are insects, spiders and worms all classified as invertebrates?

games.title: Evidence Detective
games.skillName: Using evidence to support or refute scientific ideas
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify scientific evidence that has been used to support or refute ideas or arguments; recognise that living things have changed over time and that fossils provide information about living things that inhabited the Earth millions of years ago
games.instruction: Weigh up the evidence, then tap the best answer.
games.hint: Not quite. Ask what the evidence actually shows, then try again.

questions.ask: Which evidence best shows that living things have changed over millions of years?
Fossil sea shells are found high up on mountains. What does this suggest?
Dinosaur fossils are found in much older rock than human fossils. What does this show?
Darwin saw finches with different beaks on different islands. Which idea did this support?
Some people once thought the Earth was flat. Which evidence refutes this?
Archaeopteryx fossils have feathers and teeth. They link birds to which group?
Fossils of early horses show small animals with several toes. What does this suggest?
When is a scientific idea best supported?
Mary Anning found fossils of sea creatures that no longer live. What did they help show?
Peppered moths became darker when soot covered tree bark. Which idea does this support?
